name: eventfs_iterate
prose: Precondition: file is an open eventfs directory (tracefs inode flagged TRACEFS_EVENT_INODE) and ctx is the caller's dir_context (tracefs/event_inode.c:599-713, static int eventfs_iterate(struct file *file, struct dir_context *ctx)). Postcondition: returns an int; the return statements are: 0 at line 615 if dir_emit_dots stops (the dots do not fit); -EINVAL at 619 if the inode is not an eventfs inode; and 'return ret' at 707 with ret = -EINVAL if the eventfs_inode is NULL or already freed when looked up (the lookup is under eventfs_mutex; the srcu read lock is held from line 623 and released at out), or if ei->is_freed is seen while walking the children (684); ret = 0 if the walk stops early, either because a directory entry does not fit (dir_emit false) or because ei->is_freed was set while processing the file entries (651); and ret = 1 after the whole entry list and child list have been walked (703). The function resumes from ctx->pos: c = ctx->pos - 2 entries are skipped. For each file entry from index c it calls the entry's callback under eventfs_mutex (entries whose callback returns <= 0 are skipped but ctx->pos still advances through the for-statement increment) and emits the name as DT_REG with dir_emit; when dir_emit returns false the loop exits via goto out without executing the increment, so ctx->pos is left pointing at that entry. After the file entries it subtracts the number of skipped entries from c and walks the child directories (srcu list walk): children are skipped while c > 0, then each visited child increments ctx->pos before it is checked; a freed child is skipped (ctx->pos stays incremented), and if dir_emit of a live child fails, ctx->pos is decremented again (out_dec) and the function returns 0. So ctx->pos is advanced for skipped entries as well as emitted ones, and it is not advanced for an entry whose dir_emit failed.
note: slice cut head (function at 599-713, slice 529-779). reviewers all right: original (1 is returned only after completing the iteration, 703, and 0 on a full buffer, 661/701); round 2 (ctx->pos also advances for skipped entries: callback <= 0 at 655-656 and freed children at 691-694); round 15 (the for-increment at 641 is skipped when dir_emit fails or is_freed bails out of the loop).

name: power_cut_emulated
prose: Precondition: c is a UBIFS filesystem description with c->dbg allocated and in power-cut-testing mode (dbg_is_tst_rcvry(c), checked by ubifs_assert), lnum is the logical eraseblock being accessed and write is non-zero for a write (ubifs/debug.c:2482-2574, static int power_cut_emulated(struct ubifs_info *c, int lnum, int write)). Postcondition: returns 0 (no power cut now) or 1 (a power cut is emulated: d->pc_happened is set, a warning and a stack dump are emitted). State advanced: on the first call (d->pc_cnt == 0) it randomly (1/2) chooses a delay mode: pc_delay = 1 with a random timeout of up to 60 s (pc_timeout set from jiffies) or pc_delay = 2 with pc_cnt_max random below 10000 calls, otherwise pc_delay stays unchanged (no delay), and pc_cnt is incremented. On every call it then returns 0 if pc_delay is 1 and the timeout has not passed, or if pc_delay is 2 and pc_cnt++ is still below pc_cnt_max (so in mode 2 pc_cnt advances on every call). Once past the delay it decides by LEB class with random chances, returning 0 on a 'chance' hit and otherwise logging the class and emulating the power cut: the superblock LEB (write: 1/2 skip then 19/20 skip), the master LEBs (19/20 skip), log LEBs (writes 99/100 skip, then 399/400 skip), LPT LEBs (writes 7/8 skip, then 19/20 skip), orphan LEBs (writes 1/2 skip, then 9/10 skip), the index head LEB (99/100 skip), the GC head LEB (9/10 skip), a non-bud LEB on writes when buds exist (19/20 skip), a bud LEB while a commit is running (999/1000 skip), and any other bud LEB (9999/10000 skip). The result therefore depends on random numbers and on internal state, not only on the arguments; both 0 and 1 are possible results for the same arguments, but while a delay is pending it is always 0.
note: slice cut head (function at 2482-2574, slice 2313-2569). reviewers right: original (the delay counters are advanced only in specific branches: pc_cnt at 2509 and 2515); round 2 (the delay branches 2513-2516 force 0 before the LEB class logic runs). Contract left empty (global/random state). The 'chance(a, b)' helper's exact meaning was not read; it is described only as 'a chance hit returns 0' as the code uses it.

name: lpt_gc
prose: Precondition: c is a UBIFS filesystem description with a valid LPT eraseblock table c->ltab for lpt_lebs LEBs; the caller does not hold c->lp_mutex (it is taken here) (ubifs/lpt_commit.c:1150-1169, static int lpt_gc(struct ubifs_info *c)). Postcondition: returns -ENOSPC at line 1167 if no LPT LEB was selected, else the result of lpt_gc_lnum(c, lnum) at 1168 for the selected LEB (0 on success or a negative errno from that function, not only -ENOSPC). Under c->lp_mutex it scans every LPT LEB (each entry is asserted not to be in 'tgc' state): it skips the LEB that is the node head (c->nhead_lnum) and any LEB whose free plus dirty space equals leb_size (nothing clean to preserve, so it is not worth collecting), and among the others picks the one with the largest dirty space, requiring dirty to be strictly greater than the running maximum that starts at 0; so a LEB with zero dirty space is never selected, and if every candidate has dirty == 0 (or all are skipped) the function returns -ENOSPC. The mutex is released before lpt_gc_lnum is called.
note: slice cut head (function at 1150-1169, slice 1027-1286). reviewers all right: original (lpt_gc_lnum's own errors are returned, 1168); round 2 (the skip test is free + dirty == leb_size, 1158); round 15 (the strict '>' against an initial 0 at 1160 means a zero-dirty LEB is never selected and -ENOSPC is returned).

name: mount_ubifs
prose: Precondition: c is a struct ubifs_info whose mount options have been parsed and whose volume information and vfs_sb are set (ubifs/super.c:1200-1602, static int mount_ubifs(struct ubifs_info *c); the packet name ubifs_mount does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success (line 1568, with the filesystem added to ubifs_infos and c->mounting cleared) or a negative errno at 1601 after the unwinding below. It sets ro_mount from the superblock flags and probing from SB_SILENT, then runs, with failure paths shown: init_constants_early and ubifs_debugging_init (their errors are returned directly, without cleanup labels, at 1212 and 1216); ubifs_sysfs_register (error: out_debugging); check_volume_empty; -EROFS if the volume is empty and the mount or media is read-only, or if a read-write mount is asked on read-only media (error: out_free); allocation of bottom_up_buf, sbuf, ileb_buf (read-write), write_reserve_buf (read-write) with -ENOMEM; bulk-read init; authentication init (-EINVAL if auth_key_name is set but authentication is not built in); ubifs_read_superblock (out_auth); -ENOTSUPP if the superblock's default compressor is not compiled in; init_constants_sb; allocation of cbuf and write buffers; creation of the background thread for read-write mounts; ubifs_read_master (out_master), init_constants_master, setting need_recovery if the master node is marked dirty; for a writable mount needing recovery ubifs_recover_inl_heads; ubifs_lpt_init; the space-fix-up; writing the master node with the dirty flag when no recovery is needed; the offline-signed-image HMAC update and superblock write; dbg_check_idx_size; ubifs_replay_journal (out_journal); ubifs_mount_orphans; then for read-write mounts check_free_space, a log-space check with ubifs_consolidate_log, and either recovery (ubifs_recover_size, ubifs_rcvry_gc_commit) or take_gc_lnum plus ubifs_leb_unmap of the GC LEB, and dbg_check_lprops; for read-only mounts needing recovery ubifs_recover_size, otherwise take_gc_lnum. It then adds c to the global ubifs_infos list, completes recovery for read-write mounts (need_recovery cleared) or reports it deferred for read-only ones, runs dbg_check_filesystem (error: out_infos), sets up debugfs, clears c->mounting and logs the mounted volume and geometry. Unwinding: out_infos removes c from the list; out_orphans frees orphans; out_journal destroys the journal; out_lpt frees the LPT; out_master frees the master nodes and stops the background thread; out_wbufs frees write buffers; out_cbuf frees cbuf; out_auth exits authentication; out_free frees write_reserve_buf, bulk-read buffer, ileb_buf, sbuf, bottom_up_buf, sup_node and unregisters sysfs; out_debugging exits debugging; the failure value err is returned.
note: packet name ubifs_mount does not exist; the slice 1290-1567 is the middle of mount_ubifs (super.c:1200-1602; slice cut head and tail), so FIXED under the real name. Only mechanical reviewers.

name: vboxsf_dirinfo
prose: Precondition: root is the shared-folder root id, handle an open directory handle, parsed_path is a shfl_string pattern or NULL, flags are the list flags, index the resume point (entry index to continue from), buf_len points to a u32 holding the size in bytes of the output buffer buf (a struct shfl_dirinfo area), and file_count points to a u32 (vboxsf/vboxsf_wrappers.c:250-292, int vboxsf_dirinfo(u32 root, u64 handle, struct shfl_string *parsed_path, u32 flags, u32 index, u32 *buf_len, struct shfl_dirinfo *buf, u32 *file_count); the packet name vboxsf_list does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 on success, 1 at the end of the directory, or a negative errno (per the comment at line 249); at its single return (291) both output counters are always written: *buf_len = the host-updated byte count (parms.cb) and *file_count = the number of entries returned. It fills a shfl_list parameter block (root, handle, flags, cb = *buf_len, the pattern path as a kernel input buffer or an empty input buffer when parsed_path is NULL, buf as a kernel output buffer of size *buf_len, resume_point = index, file_count = 0 as an output-only field) and calls vboxsf_call(SHFL_FN_LIST, ..., &status). If the call returned -ENODATA and the host status is VERR_NO_MORE_FILES, err becomes 1 (end of directory); any other result of vboxsf_call is returned as is. The host status value is read only when err == -ENODATA; it is not otherwise examined.

name: xfs_ag_shrink_space
prose: Precondition: pag is the last allocation group of the filesystem (ASSERT), *tpp is the caller's active transaction, delta is the number of blocks to remove from the end of the AG (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ag.c:739-873, int xfs_ag_shrink_space(struct xfs_perag *pag, struct xfs_trans **tpp, xfs_extlen_t delta)). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; *tpp may have been rolled. Early returns without any change: the error of xfs_ialloc_read_agi (764) or xfs_alloc_read_agf (770); -EFSCORRUPTED (777, with the AGF marked sick) if the AGF and AGI lengths differ; -EINVAL (780) if delta >= the AG length; the error of xfs_ialloc_check_shrink (788) if the last inode cluster could overlap the new end. Then it frees the per-AG reservation (xfs_ag_resv_free) and tries to allocate exactly the last delta blocks with xfs_alloc_vextent_exact_bno; no allocation (agbno == NULLAGBLOCK) becomes -ENOSPC. On an allocation error it holds the AGF and AGI buffers, rolls the transaction (a roll error is returned at 818 and the per-AG reservation is then NOT re-initialised), rejoins the buffers and goes to resv_init_out, which calls xfs_ag_resv_init and returns the original error if that succeeds (866-868). On success of the allocation it reduces the AGI and AGF lengths by delta and calls xfs_ag_resv_init: if that fails the lengths are restored and, when the error is not -ENOSPC, it goes to resv_err (warning 'Error %d reserving per-AG metadata reserve pool.' and xfs_force_shutdown(SHUTDOWN_CORRUPT_INCORE), returning that error, 872); when it is -ENOSPC the blocks are returned with xfs_free_extent_later (an error there also goes to resv_err), the deferred operations are finished (xfs_defer_finish; its error is returned at 850), error is set to -ENOSPC and resv_init_out runs, so a reservation that cannot be re-established gives -ENOSPC. When the reservation succeeds it updates the perag block count and inode range, logs the AGI and AGF length fields and returns 0 (863). The failure to re-initialise the per-AG reservation at resv_init_out also triggers the warning and forced shutdown (869-872), with err2 returned.
note: slice cut head (function at 739-873, slice 766-978). reviewer round 15 right: the warning and forced shutdown at resv_err (869-872) are also reached when xfs_ag_resv_init fails with a non-ENOSPC error (835-836) or when xfs_free_extent_later fails (840-841), not only from the final re-init at resv_init_out.

name: xfs_attr_set_iter
prose: Precondition: attr points to a valid xfs_attr_intent whose xattri_da_args is valid and whose xattri_dela_state names the current step of the attribute set/replace/remove state machine; called repeatedly by the deferred-operation code, once per transaction, until the state is XFS_DAS_DONE (xfs/libxfs/xfs_attr.c:810-951, int xfs_attr_set_iter(struct xfs_attr_intent *attr)). Postcondition: performs one or more steps for the current state and returns 0 (continue or done, with the state advanced) or a negative errno; the state is updated in place and is not reverted on errors, and some error returns happen after the state has changed. Return/exits by state: XFS_DAS_UNINIT: ASSERT and -EFSCORRUPTED; XFS_DAS_SF_ADD, LEAF_ADD, NODE_ADD: return xfs_attr_sf_addname, xfs_attr_leaf_addname or xfs_attr_node_addname (those set their own next state). SF_REMOVE, LEAF_REMOVE: call xfs_attr_sf_removename/xfs_attr_leaf_removename and set the state to xfs_attr_complete_op(attr, xfs_attr_init_add_state(args)) regardless of the error; the error is then returned at 950. NODE_REMOVE: xfs_attr_node_removename_setup; -ENOATTR during recovery is treated as success and completes the removal step, any other error is returned at 849 without changing the state, else the state becomes NODE_REMOVE_RMT (or the following state when there is no remote value). LEAF_SET_RMT/NODE_SET_RMT: xfs_attr_rmtval_find_space (error returned, state unchanged), state incremented, then falls through; ALLOC_RMT: xfs_attr_rmtval_alloc (error returned), and either break when the state is DONE or loop back through next_state. LEAF_REPLACE/NODE_REPLACE: xfs_attr3_leaf_flipflags (error returned) then the state is incremented. LEAF_REMOVE_OLD/NODE_REMOVE_OLD: xfs_attr_restore_rmt_blk, then, if there is a remote value, xfs_attr_rmtval_invalidate (error returned without advancing) else a first state increment, then a second increment and loop. LEAF_REMOVE_RMT/NODE_REMOVE_RMT: xfs_attr_rmtval_remove; -EAGAIN is turned into 0 and the function returns (breaks) with the state unchanged so that it is called again, other errors are returned, success increments the state. LEAF_REMOVE_ATTR: xfs_attr_leaf_remove_attr, then the state becomes the completion state whatever the result. NODE_REMOVE_ATTR: xfs_attr_node_remove_attr then, if that succeeded, xfs_attr_leaf_shrink, then the completion state. Any other state ASSERTs and falls out. At 949-950 it traces the new state and returns error.
note: slice cut head (function at 810-951, slice 783-1033). reviewers right: original (xfs_attr_rmtval_remove -EAGAIN is converted to 0 at 913-915 without advancing the state, so 'success advances the state' is not always true); round 2 (several returns, e.g. the SF/LEAF_REMOVE cases, set xattri_dela_state to the completion state even when error is non-zero, 831-837 and 933-934, 941-942, and the REMOVE_OLD/SET_RMT cases increment the state before later steps fail). Only the visible function was read; the callee functions were not.

name: xfs_bmap_add_extent_unwritten_real
prose: Precondition: tp is the running transaction, ip an inode whose fork whichfork contains an extent PREV (at the cursor icur) that fully covers the range of new and whose state (written or unwritten) differs from new->br_state; *curp is the fork's bmap btree cursor or NULL when the fork is in extent format; new has a real (non-delayed) start block (ASSERTs); logflagsp is writable (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:2008-2562, int xfs_bmap_add_extent_unwritten_real(struct xfs_trans *tp, xfs_inode_t *ip, int whichfork, struct xfs_iext_cursor *icur, struct xfs_btree_cur **curp, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *new, int *logflagsp); the item was marked dropped as not-in-slice but the function is real, and the slice 2061-2323 is its middle, slice cut head and tail). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno at the single 'return error' (2558) after the done label; *logflagsp is set to 0 at entry and ORed with the logging flags (rval, plus those from an extent-to-btree conversion) at done on every path, including failures. Method: it reads PREV and its left and right neighbours (LEFT, RIGHT) and sets state bits: LEFT_FILLING / RIGHT_FILLING when new starts / ends exactly at PREV's start / end, and LEFT_CONTIG / RIGHT_CONTIG when the neighbour is a real extent that is adjacent in file offset and disk block, has the same state as new, is on the same realtime group, and the merged length does not exceed XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN (also for the all-three-merged case). It then handles these combinations: (1) fills all of PREV and merges with both neighbours (removes two incore extents, updates LEFT; with a btree cursor it deletes RIGHT and PREV records and updates LEFT); (2) fills all of PREV and merges left; (3) fills all of PREV and merges right; (4) fills all of PREV with no merge (changes PREV's state); (5) fills the first part of PREV and merges left; (6) fills the first part with no merge (PREV shrinks and new is inserted before it); (7) fills the last part and merges right; (8) fills the last part with no merge; (9) fills a middle part (PREV is split into three, increasing the extent count by 2). The cases with a contiguity bit but not matching a filling pattern (LEFT_FILLING|LEFT_CONTIG|RIGHT_CONTIG, RIGHT_FILLING|LEFT_CONTIG|RIGHT_CONTIG, LEFT_FILLING|RIGHT_CONTIG, RIGHT_FILLING|LEFT_CONTIG, LEFT_CONTIG|RIGHT_CONTIG, LEFT_CONTIG, RIGHT_CONTIG) are impossible (ASSERT(0)). With a btree cursor each case does record lookups, deletes, updates and inserts: a lookup that does not find the expected record (i != 1, or i != 0 for an insert position) marks the btree sick and gives -EFSCORRUPTED, and any btree call error goes to done; the in-memory extent list and if_nextents were already changed before these btree operations, so an error leaves them updated. After the switch it records the rmap change (xfs_rmap_convert_extent), converts the fork to a btree if now needed (xfs_bmap_extents_to_btree, whose error goes to done), clears cur->bc_bmap.allocated and stores *curp.

Helper functions (xfs_btree_* and xfs_iext_*) were not read.

name: xfs_bmap_extsize_align
prose: Precondition: mp is the mount; gotp is the extent after the request (it may be the end-of-file record) and prevp the extent before it (offset NULLFILEOFF when there is none); extsz is the extent size hint and must be non-zero (it is a divisor); rt, eof, delay and convert are flags; offp and lenp point to the requested file offset and length (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:2817-2988, static int xfs_bmap_extsize_align(xfs_mount_t *mp, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *gotp, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *prevp, xfs_extlen_t extsz, int rt, int eof, int delay, int convert, xfs_fileoff_t *offp, xfs_extlen_t *lenp); the packet name xfs_file_alloc_size_align does not exist). Postcondition: returns 0 with *offp and *lenp adjusted, or -EINVAL with them unchanged; the return statements are 0 at 2839 (convert is set: nothing is changed), 0 at 2852 (the request lies entirely inside gotp and neither delay nor eof is set: unchanged), -EINVAL at 2945 and 2970 (realtime only) and 0 at 2987 with the new values stored. Computation: it rounds the start down to a multiple of extsz (extending the length by the amount moved), rounds the length up to a multiple of extsz, and reduces the length by extsz steps while it exceeds XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN. It then moves the start forward to the end of the previous extent if the aligned start (when it was moved) lies before it, moves the start back so the end does not run into the next extent (not before offset 0), repeats the previous-extent check, and, if the end still overlaps the next extent, shortens the length to end exactly at the next extent. For a realtime inode whose resulting length is not a multiple of the realtime extent size it removes blocks by moving the start up, or pulling the end in, or trimming the length, and returns -EINVAL if the result would not cover the original request [orig_off, orig_end) (checked at 2942-2945 and 2969-2970); for non-realtime inodes the cover property is only ASSERTed (debug builds), including an allowance when the length was cut to XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN, so the result may not cover the whole original request in that case. The function takes no locks or references and only writes *offp and *lenp.
note: packet name xfs_file_alloc_size_align does not exist; the described function is xfs_bmap_extsize_align (xfs_bmap.c:2817-2988); the slice 2841-3141 starts inside it (slice cut head). Mechanical reviewers only. The earlier prose said the result always covers the original request; for non-realtime inodes that is only asserted (2972-2975), and the length can be capped at XFS_MAX_BMBT_EXTLEN (2881-2882), so it is qualified here.

name: xfs_bmap_del_extent_real
prose: Precondition: ip is an inode, tp the running transaction, icur an extent cursor positioned at the extent got that fully contains del, cur is the bmap btree cursor or NULL when the fork is in extent format, del is the non-empty range being removed (must satisfy got.br_startoff <= del->br_startoff and got's end >= del's end, ASSERTed), logflagsp is writable, whichfork is the fork, bflags the XFS_BMAPI_* flags (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:4909-5162, int xfs_bmap_del_extent_real(xfs_inode_t *ip, xfs_trans_t *tp, struct xfs_iext_cursor *icur, struct xfs_btree_cur *cur, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *del, int *logflagsp, int whichfork, uint32_t bflags)). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno; *logflagsp is zeroed at entry, set to XFS_ILOG_CORE once past the early check and OR-ed with the fork's extent logging flag when no btree is used. Early returns: -ENOSPC at 4961 when the transaction has no block reservation (t_blk_res == 0), the fork is in extent format at its maximum extent count and del is strictly inside got (so the removal would split the extent and force a btree conversion), with *logflagsp still 0; with a cursor, the result of xfs_bmbt_lookup_eq(cur, &got) is returned if it fails and -EFSCORRUPTED (btree marked sick) if the record is not found (4972-4978). By how del sits in got: whole extent (the incore entry is removed and if_nextents decremented; with a cursor xfs_btree_delete, a miss gives -EFSCORRUPTED); first part (got is moved up and shortened; btree record updated); last part (got shortened; btree record updated); middle (got shortened to the part before del, a new extent for the part after is inserted; with a cursor the record is updated, the cursor incremented and the new record inserted: an -ENOSPC from the insert is undone by re-looking up got, restoring the original btree record and incore extent, setting *logflagsp = 0 and returning -ENOSPC; other errors are returned as is and an insert miss gives -EFSCORRUPTED). Btree operations are only done when cur is non-NULL. After the switch it removes the reverse mapping (xfs_rmap_unmap_extent) and, unless XFS_BMAPI_REMAP is set, schedules the blocks to be freed: refcount decrease for a reflink inode's data fork, xfs_bmap_free_rtblocks for a realtime fork without rtgroups, otherwise xfs_free_extent_later (with SKIP_DISCARD for NODISCARD or unwritten extents, and the REALTIME flag for realtime); an error from the free step is returned (5147). Finally it subtracts the block count from ip->i_nblocks and, unless REMAP, adjusts the quota (realtime or normal block count) and returns 0.

Helper functions were not read.

name: xfs_bmap_del_extent_real
prose: Precondition: ip is an inode, tp the running transaction, icur an extent cursor positioned at the extent got that fully contains del, cur is the bmap btree cursor or NULL when the fork is in extent format, del is the non-empty range being removed (must satisfy got.br_startoff <= del->br_startoff and got's end >= del's end, ASSERTed), logflagsp is writable, whichfork is the fork, bflags the XFS_BMAPI_* flags (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:4909-5162, int xfs_bmap_del_extent_real(xfs_inode_t *ip, xfs_trans_t *tp, struct xfs_iext_cursor *icur, struct xfs_btree_cur *cur, xfs_bmbt_irec_t *del, int *logflagsp, int whichfork, uint32_t bflags)). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno; *logflagsp is zeroed at entry, set to XFS_ILOG_CORE once past the early check and OR-ed with the fork's extent logging flag when no btree is used. Early returns: -ENOSPC at 4961 when the transaction has no block reservation (t_blk_res == 0), the fork is in extent format at its maximum extent count and del is strictly inside got (so the removal would split the extent and force a btree conversion), with *logflagsp still 0; with a cursor, the result of xfs_bmbt_lookup_eq(cur, &got) is returned if it fails and -EFSCORRUPTED (btree marked sick) if the record is not found (4972-4978). By how del sits in got: whole extent (the incore entry is removed and if_nextents decremented; with a cursor xfs_btree_delete, a miss gives -EFSCORRUPTED); first part (got is moved up and shortened; btree record updated); last part (got shortened; btree record updated); middle (got shortened to the part before del, a new extent for the part after is inserted; with a cursor the record is updated, the cursor incremented and the new record inserted: an -ENOSPC from the insert is undone by re-looking up got, restoring the original btree record and incore extent, setting *logflagsp = 0 and returning -ENOSPC; other errors are returned as is and an insert miss gives -EFSCORRUPTED). Btree operations are only done when cur is non-NULL. After the switch it removes the reverse mapping (xfs_rmap_unmap_extent) and, unless XFS_BMAPI_REMAP is set, schedules the blocks to be freed: refcount decrease for a reflink inode's data fork, xfs_bmap_free_rtblocks for a realtime fork without rtgroups, otherwise xfs_free_extent_later (with SKIP_DISCARD for NODISCARD or unwritten extents, and the REALTIME flag for realtime); an error from the free step is returned (5147). Finally it subtracts the block count from ip->i_nblocks and, unless REMAP, adjusts the quota (realtime or normal block count) and returns 0.
note: packet name xfs_bmap_del_extent does not exist in xfs_bmap.c (the delete helpers are xfs_bmap_del_extent_delay at 4662, xfs_bmap_del_extent_cow at 4806 and xfs_bmap_del_extent_real at 4909); the item's earlier prose (del lies wholly inside got, del's start block is not a delalloc start block, cur may be NULL) matches xfs_bmap_del_extent_real, whose body ends at xfs_bmap.c:5162 inside this slice (4934-5196), so it is FIXED under that name with the same prose as the previous record (they describe the same function). The slice also contains the start of __xfs_bunmapi (5171), which is not this item.

name: __xfs_bunmapi
prose: Precondition: tp is the running transaction, ip an inode with XFS_ILOCK_EXCL held (asserted), start is the first file offset to remove, rlen points to the length to unmap (len > 0, asserted), flags are XFS_BMAPI_* flags (the fork is chosen with xfs_bmapi_whichfork and must not be the COW fork), nexts is the maximum number of extents to remove or 0 for no limit (xfs/libxfs/xfs_bmap.c:5171-5465, static int __xfs_bunmapi(struct xfs_trans *tp, struct xfs_inode *ip, xfs_fileoff_t start, xfs_filblks_t *rlen, uint32_t flags, xfs_extnum_t nexts); the packet name xfs_bunmapi is the exported wrapper, the code in the slice is this function). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno at line 5464 (or earlier returns); *rlen is set to the amount still to be unmapped (0 when done). Early returns (before *rlen is written except where noted): -EFSCORRUPTED (5204, fork marked sick) if the fork should have extents but has none; -EIO (5207) if the filesystem is shut down; the xfs_iread_extents error (5215); 0 with *rlen = 0 (5219) if the fork has no extents; 0 with *rlen = 0 (5227) if no extent lies before the end of the range. Otherwise it starts a bmap btree cursor when the fork is in btree format and walks extents backward from the end of the range while the offset has not passed start and fewer than nexts extents were processed: it trims the found extent to the range (del), and for realtime forms (without XFS_BMAPI_REMAP) handles partial realtime extents: skipping unwritten pieces that are not extent-aligned, converting a written piece to unwritten with xfs_bmap_add_extent_unwritten_real, or unwriting part of the previous extent; any error from those goes to error0. Aligned ranges go to delete: a delayed-allocation extent uses xfs_bmap_del_extent_delay, a real one xfs_bmap_del_extent_real (error: error0, with the partial logflags merged). After the loop *rlen is set to 0 if done, if end reached -1 or fell below start, else end - start + 1 (this assignment happens before the fork format conversion, so *rlen is already set when the conversion fails, as the round-15 reviewer said). It then converts the fork to a btree if now required (xfs_bmap_extents_to_btree) or back to extents when possible (xfs_bmap_btree_to_extents), whose error is returned. error0 trims the inode logging flags to match the final fork format, logs the inode if any flag remains (even on error, so a dirty transaction can be shut down), and frees the cursor (setting bc_bmap.allocated = 0 only on success). Note that the error0 path taken from the middle of the loop leaves *rlen at its input value.
note: packet name xfs_bunmapi does not match the code: the function containing the slice is __xfs_bunmapi (xfs_bmap.c:5171-5465; slice 5197-5466 starts near its beginning, slice cut head). reviewer round 15 right: *rlen is assigned at 5424-5427 before the conversion at 5432-5440, so a conversion error still returns with *rlen set; errors from the loop jump to error0 earlier and do not update *rlen.

name: xfbtree_trans_commit
prose: Precondition: xfbt is an in-memory (xfile-backed) btree and tp a transaction whose t_items list may hold log items for buffers of that btree (xfs/libxfs/xfs_btree_mem.c:269-313, int xfbtree_trans_commit(struct xfbtree *xfbt, struct xfs_trans *tp)). Postcondition: returns 0 or the first error from xmbuf_finalize (a verification or write-out failure of one of the btree's buffers); the single return is 'return error' at 312. It walks every log item of tp (list_for_each_entry_safe); for items that do not belong to xfbt (xfbtree_buf_match returns NULL) it only records whether the item is dirty (tp_dirty) and continues; for each matching buffer it detaches the buffer from the transaction (xmbuf_trans_bdetach), finalises it with xmbuf_finalize only while no error has yet been recorded (after the first error the remaining buffers are still detached and released but not finalised), and releases it with xfs_buf_relse, so all of the btree's buffers are removed from the transaction even after an error. Finally it resets tp->t_flags' XFS_TRANS_DIRTY bit to match the dirty state of the log items that remain attached (set if any non-btree item is dirty, else cleared) and returns the recorded error.
note: slice cut head (function at 269-313, slice 277-348). Unreviewed originally; verified against the source.

name: xfs_da3_node_lookup_int
prose: Precondition: state is an initialised xfs_da_state whose args (with dp, trans, whichfork, geo, hashval, owner) is valid, state->path is empty, and result points to an int (xfs/libxfs/xfs_da_btree.c:1677-1884, int xfs_da3_node_lookup_int(struct xfs_da_state *state, int *result)). Postcondition: returns 0 with *result set, or a negative errno (the result is not written on an errno return); the returns are: the xfs_da3_node_read error at 1719 (with blk->blkno cleared and path.active decremented back first), -EFSCORRUPTED at 1730, 1743, 1754, 1761, 1777, 1786, 1839, 1845 and 1865 for header-check failures, an unrecognised block magic, a node level of XFS_DA_NODE_MAXDEPTH or more, a level that is not one less than the parent's, an interior entry pointing back to the root block, a leaf level reached at the wrong expected level, or a leaf that is neither a dir2 leafn nor an attribute leaf (in these corruption cases state->path.active is not decremented, unlike the read-error case), the xfs_da3_path_shift error at 1872, and 0 at 1883. The function descends from args->geo->leafblk, reading each block (up to XFS_DA_NODE_MAXDEPTH levels), recording blk->blkno, blk->magic, blk->hashval and, for interior nodes, the chosen blk->index found by a binary search for the first entry whose hashval is not below args->hashval (the last entry when all are smaller). At the leaf it calls xfs_dir2_leafn_lookup_int or xfs_attr3_leaf_lookup_int, whose result becomes retval: 0 when the entry was found, -ENOENT (or -ENOATTR for attribute leaves) when it was not found, so *result = 0 means found and a negative value means not found, not the reverse. If the lookup says not found but the leaf's last hashval equals the search hashval it shifts the path to the next leaf (xfs_da3_path_shift) and searches again, repeating while the shift succeeds; an attribute lookup that runs out of leaves gets -ENOATTR. state->path.active records the number of levels read.
note: slice cut head (function at 1677-1884, slice 1550-1811). reviewers: round 1 right (the corruption returns do not decrement path.active, only the read-error return does, 1718); round 2 right (*result is 0 on found and -ENOENT/-ENOATTR on not found, 1867-1882). The earlier text that the result semantic was the opposite is corrected. Contract left empty (pointer arguments and structure state).

name: xfs_dir_rename_children
prose: Precondition: tp is the running transaction, du_src = (src_dp, src_name, src_ip) is the existing entry, du_tgt = (target_dp, target_name, target_ip) is the destination (target_ip NULL when it does not exist), du_wip describes the optional whiteout inode (du_wip->ip NULL if none), spaceres is the block reservation (0 means none); all inodes have ILOCK held; if src_ip is a directory its '..' does not already point to target_dp and a whiteout inode is freshly allocated with i_nlink 0 (xfs/libxfs/xfs_dir2.c:1187-1412, int xfs_dir_rename_children(struct xfs_trans *tp, struct xfs_dir_update *du_src, struct xfs_dir_update *du_tgt, unsigned int spaceres, struct xfs_dir_update *du_wip); the packet name xfs_rename belongs to xfs_inode.c and is not this function). Postcondition: returns 0, or the negative errno of the first failing step; steps done before an error are not undone, so after the point where the transaction is dirtied the caller must cancel it with a shutdown, except for the two 'expected error' checks done first. Return points: -EEXIST at 1230 if the target exists, is a directory and is not empty or has i_nlink > 2; the xfs_dir_canenter error at 1219 when the target does not exist and spaceres is 0 (both before anything is dirtied); then errors from, in order: xfs_iunlink_remove of the whiteout inode (it is then linked with xfs_bumplink); creating the target entry with xfs_dir_createname (or, if the target exists, replacing it with xfs_dir_replace and dropping a link on target_ip, twice if src_ip is a directory); for a directory moved to a different parent, rewriting its '..' entry with xfs_dir_replace; dropping a link on src_dp when src_ip is a directory and (the parent changed or the target existed); replacing the source entry with the whiteout inode (xfs_dir_replace) or removing it (xfs_dir_removename); the parent-pointer updates (xfs_parent_addname for the whiteout, xfs_parent_replacename for the source, xfs_parent_removename for the target) when ppargs are present; 0 at 1411. On the way it bumps the link count of target_dp for a new directory entry that crosses directories, updates ctime/mtime of the target and source parents and the ctime of src_ip, and logs the inodes. At the end it calls the xfs_dir_update_hook callbacks: removal of the target (if any) and of the source, creation of the target entry for src_ip and of the whiteout entry (if any), in that order.
note: packet name xfs_rename does not exist in xfs_dir2.c; the function in this slice (1273-1412) is the second half of xfs_dir_rename_children (xfs_dir2.c:1187-1412; slice cut head). Fixed under the real name. Mechanical reviewers only.

name: xfs_dir2_sf_to_block
prose: Precondition: args holds a valid transaction (args->trans), geometry and the directory inode args->dp, which has a shortform (XFS_DINODE_FMT_LOCAL) data fork with no extents and with if_bytes equal to i_disk_size (ASSERTed) (xfs/libxfs/xfs_dir2_block.c:1076-1281, int xfs_dir2_sf_to_block(struct xfs_da_args *args)). Postcondition: returns 0 with the directory converted to a single data block in block format, or a negative errno. It copies the shortform data to a temporary buffer (kmalloc with __GFP_NOFAIL), empties the in-core inode data and the fork (xfs_idata_realloc, xfs_bmap_local_to_extents_empty, i_disk_size = 0) and then: adds block 0 with xfs_dir2_grow_inode, initialises it as a data block (xfs_dir3_data_init) and as a block-format block (xfs_dir3_block_init), reserves the leaf and tail area at the end with xfs_dir2_data_use_free, sets the tail count to sfp->count + 2, claims the remaining free space, writes the '.' entry (inode args->owner) and the '..' entry (parent inode from the shortform header), then copies each shortform entry to its original offset (inserting unused-space holes where the offsets have gaps, so the existing offsets are preserved), computing and storing each leaf hash and data pointer, frees the temporary buffer, sorts the leaf entries by hash (xfs_sort), logs the leaf area and the tail, runs xfs_dir3_data_check and returns 0 (line 1277). The errors of xfs_dir2_grow_inode, xfs_dir3_data_init and the two xfs_dir2_data_use_free calls go to out_free, which frees the temporary buffer and returns the error (1280); at that point the in-core shortform data has already been discarded, so the directory is left empty and the transaction dirty (the caller must cancel it).
note: slice cut head (function at 1076-1281, slice 1107-1281). Unreviewed originally; verified against the full function. The statement that the failed-conversion directory is left empty reads from lines 1122-1124 happening before any of the failing calls.

name: xfs_dir2_leafn_remove
prose: Precondition: args (with trans, geo, dp, owner, total) is valid, bp is the locked, joined leaf buffer, index is the index of the leaf entry to remove, dblk is the state block of the data block holding that entry (dblk->blkno and dblk->index match the entry's data block and offset, ASSERTed), rval points to an int (xfs/libxfs/xfs_dir2_node.c:1271-1422, int xfs_dir2_leafn_remove(xfs_da_args_t *args, struct xfs_buf *bp, int index, xfs_da_state_blk_t *dblk, int *rval)). Postcondition: returns 0 with *rval set at 1418, or a negative errno without writing *rval. It marks the leaf entry stale (address set to XFS_DIR2_NULL_DATAPTR, stale count incremented, header and entry logged), makes the data entry free in the data block (xfs_dir2_data_make_free; rescans and logs the data header if needed). If that increased the longest free run in the data block, it reads the free block (xfs_dir2_free_read; its error is returned at 1366), and if the data block is now entirely empty (longest == blksize - data_entry_offset) it tries xfs_dir2_shrink_inode: on success dblk->bp is cleared; an -ENOSPC with no space reservation (args->total == 0) is tolerated (the empty block is left for someone else to remove); any other error is returned at 1401. It then updates the free block with xfs_dir3_data_block_free (error returned at 1410). Finally it checks the leaf and sets *rval to true when leaf_hdr_size + sizeof(leafhdr.ents) * (count - stale) < geo->magicpct, i.e. when the leaf is small enough to try joining with a neighbour; note the multiplier is sizeof(leafhdr.ents), the size of the in-core entries pointer, not the size of one on-disk leaf entry (as the round-15 reviewer observed), so the threshold is computed with that size.
note: slice cut head (function at 1271-1422, slice 1294-1562). reviewer round 15 right: xfs_dir2_node.c:1419 uses sizeof(leafhdr.ents) (a pointer size), not sizeof(xfs_dir2_leaf_entry_t); the previous annotation claim about the leaf entry size is replaced by the literal expression.

name: xfs_bui_log_format_sizeof
prose: Precondition: nr is the number of extent records (unsigned int) that follow the header of an xfs_bui_log_format log item (xfs/libxfs/xfs_log_format.h:869-875, static inline size_t xfs_bui_log_format_sizeof(unsigned int nr)). Postcondition: returns sizeof(struct xfs_bui_log_format) + nr * sizeof(struct xfs_map_extent) at line 873-874, computed in size_t arithmetic: the byte size of the fixed header followed by nr map-extent records. The numeric struct sizes (header and per-record) are defined by the structure layouts in the header and are not restated here: the earlier claims of 16 + 24 * nr and 16 bytes per record were not verified and reviewers disagreed (16, 24 or 32 bytes per record), so the prose names the sizeof expressions only. The function reads and writes no state.
note: slice cut head (function at 869-875, slice 791-1043). Contract left empty because the structure sizes are not stated in the source slice; the round 1 and round 15 reviewers' point (the 24-byte figure is unverified) is accepted and the number is removed.

name: xfs_refcount_merge_center_extents
prose: Precondition: cur is a refcount btree cursor; left, center and right describe three adjacent extents in the same refcount domain (ASSERTed) that are to be merged into left, with center's range possibly synthesised rather than stored; extlen is the combined length; aglen points to the remaining length to process (xfs/libxfs/xfs_refcount.c:486-562, static int xfs_refcount_merge_center_extents(struct xfs_btree_cur *cur, struct xfs_refcount_irec *left, struct xfs_refcount_irec *center, struct xfs_refcount_irec *right, unsigned long long extlen, xfs_extlen_t *aglen)). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; on success it has removed the center and right records from the btree (the first delete, preceded by a lookup_ge at center's start block, removes the center record or, if center was synthesised, the right record; a second delete happens only when center->rc_refcount > 1, i.e. when the center record is actually stored, so the center is not always deleted), set left->rc_blockcount = extlen, updated the left record (found by lookup_le at left's start block), and set *aglen = 0 (line 556). Each lookup or delete that finds no record (found_rec != 1) marks the btree sick and gives -EFSCORRUPTED, and any btree call error is returned; all failures go to out_error, which only traces and returns the error, so *aglen is unchanged and earlier deletions are not undone. The structure left is modified in memory (blockcount) before xfs_refcount_update is called.
note: slice cut head (function at 486-562, slice 520-783). reviewer round 15 right: the second delete is conditional on center->rc_refcount > 1 (xfs_refcount.c:529-538), the comment at 502-508 explains the synthesised-center case.

name: xfs_rmap_convert
prose: Precondition: cur is the rmap btree cursor (caller has the btree to itself), bno and len are the AG block range being converted, unwritten says the CURRENT state of the extent is unwritten (the call flips it), oinfo describes an inode data-fork owner (not a non-inode owner, attr-fork or bmbt-block owner: ASSERTed); an existing record PREV of the current state with PREV.rm_startblock <= bno must contain the whole range (PREV.rm_offset <= offset, ASSERTed, and PREV.rm_offset + PREV.rm_blockcount >= offset + len), where offset is the file offset unpacked from oinfo (xfs/libxfs/xfs_rmap.c:1248-1738, int xfs_rmap_convert(struct xfs_btree_cur *cur, xfs_agblock_t bno, xfs_extlen_t len, bool unwritten, const struct xfs_owner_info *oinfo)). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno; the single return is 'return error' at 1737 (after tracing the error). It looks up PREV with xfs_rmap_lookup_le (-EFSCORRUPTED if not found), sets RMAP_LEFT_FILLING / RIGHT_FILLING when PREV begins / ends exactly at the converted range (PREV.rm_offset == offset is only required for LEFT_FILLING; a PREV that starts earlier is allowed and gives the split cases), reads the left and right neighbouring records (a neighbour overlapping the range gives -EFSCORRUPTED) and sets LEFT_CONTIG / RIGHT_CONTIG when they are adjacent in block and file offset and mergeable with the new state (xfs_rmap_is_mergeable), clearing RIGHT_CONTIG when the merged length of all three would exceed XFS_RMAP_LEN_MAX. After repositioning the cursor on PREV it applies one of nine cases: all of PREV converted and merged with both neighbours (delete RIGHT and PREV, update LEFT); all of PREV with left merge; all of PREV with right merge; all of PREV with no merge (flags flipped); first part with left merge; first part without merge (PREV shrinks, new record inserted); last part with right merge; last part without merge; middle part (PREV is split: the right remainder updated, the left remainder and the middle new-state record inserted). The seven combinations with a CONTIG bit that are inconsistent with the FILLING bits are impossible (ASSERT(0), no handling). Each lookup/increment/decrement/delete/insert that does not find or create the expected record (i != 1, or i != 0 for an insert position) marks the btree sick and returns -EFSCORRUPTED, and any btree call error goes to done; operations already done before an error are not undone.
note: slice cut head (function at 1248-1738, slice 1290-1551). reviewer round 15 right: the code asserts PREV.rm_offset <= offset (xfs_rmap.c:1294), not equality; only LEFT_FILLING (equality at 1303) uses equality to choose the case.
